Forgetting about draws too. The 5 ways a game can end in a draw:
Stalemate: King isn't in check and player cannot move
Insufficient material: Three board positions where checkmate cannot happen to either player:
- White king and black king
- White king, black king, any color bishop (1x)
- White king, black king, any color knight (1x)
Fifty-move rule: No pawn moves or captures in the last 50 moves for each player (100 moves in total).

Threefold repetition: EXACT same board position (including colors) three times in a row with the same legal moves each time (including castling and en passant). Doesn't matter if two pieces switched spots.\nAgreement: each player agrees to a draw (very common).
About castling: King and rook may not have moved before.
